item.title: ‘She was struggling to breathe’: Federal agents pepper-spray 1-year-old girl in Chicago’s Little Village — video
item.description: US Border Patrol agents pepper-sprayed Rafael Veraza and his one-year-old daughter in a Sam's Club parking lot, days after a judge tightened rules on agent use of force. The Department of Homeland Security claims agents faced gunfire and vehicle rammings, but offered no explanation for the spray incident.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Exposing corrupt journalists': Donald Trump reacts to BBC boss Tim Davie stepping down over Jan 6 speech row
item.description: Donald Trump thanked The Telegraph for exposing what he called "corrupt journalists" at the BBC following the resignation of Director-General Tim Davie. Trump alleged the BBC doctored his January 6th speech to appear to encourage violence, accusing the broadcaster of trying to influence a US presidential election.

item.title: Former Prince Andrew brought prostitutes to Buckingham Palace ‘on a regular basis’; Queen Elizabeth was aware, claims historian
item.description: Historian Andrew Lownie alleges Prince Andrew used Buckingham Palace as a 'pleasure palace' with prostitutes, with Queen Elizabeth aware but taking no action due to him being her favorite son. Former staff, no longer fearing reprisal after Andrew's removal from power, are now speaking out about his alleged misconduct, including a reported incident involving 40 prostitutes in Thailand.

item.title: Why did BBC director-general Tim Davie resign? Inside the row over doctored Trump January 6 speech
item.description: BBC Director-General Tim Davie has resigned after 20 years, citing intense demands and admitting to mistakes, including a controversial Trump documentary edit. This departure follows accusations of systemic bias in coverage of the Gaza conflict and transgender issues, placing the BBC's impartiality under scrutiny.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: UFC legend Rampage Jackson’s Rome livestream turns chaotic after fake money giveaway
item.description: Former UFC champion Quinton “Rampage” Jackson's livestream stunt in Rome took a chaotic turn when he distributed fake money in a busy tourist area. A surge of street vendors and hustlers rushed to grab the prop bills, creating a tense scene that forced Jackson to retreat. The incident highlights the unpredictable nature of public content creation in bustling urban environments.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: Who is Tea Tyme? TikToker accused of hitting Zion man during live stream as shocking clip goes viral
item.description: TikTok creator Ty Nesha, known as Tea Tyme, is under scrutiny after reportedly hitting and killing a pedestrian, Darren Lucas, while livestreaming. The incident occurred in Zion, Illinois, and Nesha remained at the scene, cooperating with authorities. The investigation into the fatal crash is ongoing, with no charges yet announced.
item.dc:creator: Sehjal Gupta

item.title: BBC director-general Tim Davie quits after 20 years amid row over misleading edit of Trump’s January 6 speech
item.description: BBC director-general Tim Davie and News CEO Deborah Turness have resigned following a major controversy over a Panorama documentary. The program allegedly misedited Donald Trump's speech, making it seem he intended to march on the US Capitol. An internal dossier revealed editorial failures, sparking widespread anger and prompting calls for accountability.

item.title: SNL’s ‘Trump’ butchers Usha Vance’s name in chaotic Oval Office spoof — watch full video
item.description: Saturday Night Live's cold open featured James Austin Johnson as Donald Trump during a meeting about GLP-1 medications. When a staffer fainted, Trump's character made jokes, mocked RFK Jr.'s reaction, and then pivoted to political commentary on rising prices, government shutdowns, and even stealing Christmas.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Federal agents detain and separate Latino father from toddler, leaving child with ‘dirty diaper, bruises and rash’; DHS justifies actions
item.description: A Latino father's arrest and separation from his toddler in Los Angeles has sparked outrage. The child was found distressed with a dirty diaper and a bruise. Federal agents deny misconduct, claiming the father endangered the child by confronting them with a hammer. Governor Newsom condemned the handling of the toddler, while DHS defended the agents' actions.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Worst President in US history': Trump slams 'sleepy, crooked' Biden; blames him for 'disasters pushing nation to brink of destruction'
item.description: Donald Trump declared Joe Biden the "worst President in American history," citing economic decline, border security failures, and a "humiliating" Afghanistan withdrawal. Trump accused Biden of being "dominated by radical handlers" and "weaponising law enforcement" against political opponents, asserting that Biden's perceived weakness emboldened global adversaries.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Top 10 richest people in the world 2025: How Elon Musk nears trillionaire status and dominates global wealth rankings
item.description: Elon Musk is the world's richest person in November 2025. Technology leaders and business magnates dominate the top wealth rankings. Musk's ventures in electric vehicles, space, and AI have propelled him to the forefront. He is on track to become the first trillionaire. Other prominent figures include Larry Ellison, Jeff Bezos, Larry Page, and Mark Zuckerberg.

item.title: YouTuber Candace Owens fires back at Ben Shapiro after he claims she accused Erika Kirk of killing Charlie Kirk
item.description: Candace Owens vehemently denied accusing Erika Kirk of her husband Charlie Kirk's death, calling Ben Shapiro a liar for his claims on The Megyn Kelly Show. Owens stated Shapiro fabricated the accusation to discredit her. Meanwhile, Erika Kirk appealed for public grace following her husband's passing, emphasizing the impact of online discourse on her children.
item.dc:creator: Sehjal Gupta

item.title: ‘USAID and Clinton’: Ex-B'desh minister alleges US-backed plot to topple Hasina;
item.description: A former Bangladeshi minister alleges USAID and the Bill Clinton family backed the 2024 riots that ousted Sheikh Hasina. He claims US organisations, including USAID and IRI, funded campaigns to destabilise the Awami League government. Hasina, now in India, also accused the US of involvement, a claim the White House denies.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Vladimir Putin did not order nuclear test, Russia reiterates
item.description: Russia denies ordering nuclear tests, reaffirming its commitment to a moratorium. Moscow warns it will reciprocate if the US conducts tests, emphasizing nuclear parity for global security. Meanwhile, Russia awaits a US response on extending strategic weapons freeze, a proposal aimed at maintaining stability.

item.title: 'People against tariffs are fools': Trump slams US Supreme Court; cites 'record investment'
item.description: President Donald Trump strongly defended his tariff policies. He stated these measures have enriched America and made it the world's most respected nation. The US Supreme Court is currently reviewing the president's authority to impose import duties. Trump argued that tariffs are essential for national security and economic prosperity. The court's decision could significantly impact future presidential trade powers.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Charlie Kirk's leaked messages show Ben Shapiro’s jealousy toward YouTuber Candace Owens as feud explodes online
item.description: Leaked texts reveal Charlie Kirk believed Ben Shapiro sought to sabotage his and Candace Owens' careers. Amidst this, Shapiro accused Owens of making "vile" claims, including alleging TPUSA insiders were involved in Kirk's death. Owens vehemently denied this, calling Shapiro a liar. Erika Kirk, Charlie's widow, urged caution with online speculation.
item.dc:creator: Sehjal Gupta
